title: Native mission counters, timers and terminal event lifecycle
status: Research and MissionFeatures implementation frozen; no IDB, UI or game-process changes
scope: YS field missions; excludes Gummi mission HUD/state. Builds on world_camera/native_retry without claiming every external mission BDX or asset was enumerated.

implementation.result: 1092 synthetic checks, zero failures, MSVC /W4 no warnings; no game code executed
implementation.behavior: Two one-shot native timer actions; counter/gauge/score/lifecycle readouts. No retained pointers or periodic writes.

evidence_audit.qualification: Counts describe collected complete functions, not a coverage percentage or exhaustiveness guarantee.

claims.Finding: RCX is Mission*, EDX unsigned mission ID, R8 filename token. Constructor builds msn/<language>/<token>.bar; initializes one timer+296, three counters+352 with stride80, three gauges+592 with stride72, watch+808, combo counter+880, score+1088, phase+1072=0 and Drive factor+1704=1. The decompiler's apparent two-argument prototype omits R8.
claims.Limitations: The resource token and ID list are external mission data. Constructor flags1 alone do not establish widget configuration.

claims.Finding: Reconstructs the mission in static storage RVA2A0F8B0 and publishes the returned pointer in RVA2A0FF68. The incoming filename in RDX becomes constructor R8.
claims.Limitations: Pointer equality alone is not a lifetime/generation token; identical missions can reuse storage.

claims.Finding: Attaches loaded BAR at Mission+96, obtains BAR type2 descriptor into Mission+8 and mirror RVA2A0FF70, and translates descriptor flags1/20/40/80/100 into native control state.
claims.Limitations: Missing BAR entries can be dereferenced in native code; not an arbitrary trainer loader API.

claims.Finding: Parses descriptor commands beginning at+28, loads optional BAR type3 script/type18 effects, starts presentation and registers3A35C0 as group1 priority14000 task.
claims.Limitations: This owns resources and task allocation; not reused by timer actions.

claims.Finding: Descriptor opcode4 configures timer;5 counter;6 gauge;7 combo;8 score;9 watch. Opcode11 stores mission Drivefactor+1704;12 adjusts current Drive through native status helper.
claims.Limitations: Record IDs and lengths are not bounds-checked by these dispatch arms; loaded resources are an engine trust assumption.

claims.Finding: Initializes the specified widget through vtable+8, configures start/max/threshold through+48, optionally attaches BAR HUD resources, appends widget to Mission+976 registry and increments count+1048.
claims.Limitations: Registry capacity is nine pointers before count1048. Trainer independently rejects out-of-bounds, duplicate or foreign entries.

claims.Finding: Counter descriptor index at record+19 selects Mission+352+80*index.
claims.Limitations: Trainer accepts only the three statically constructed counters.

claims.Finding: Gauge descriptor index selects Mission+592+72*index, configures it and calls3FA310 with float-converted initial value.
claims.Limitations: Initialization itself can follow setter threshold behavior. Trainer does not call it.

claims.Finding: Timer descriptor index selects Mission+296+56*index.
claims.Limitations: Only one timer is constructed; trainer requires index0, exact timer vtable and registry membership.

claims.Finding: Default base widget reset sets flags1, ID fromEDX, max0, sound0 and UI resource null.
claims.Limitations: Unused inline widgets therefore still have bit1; publishing their old +56 fields without registry/ID checks would be wrong.

claims.Finding: Activates each registered widget via vtable+16 except objects with flag0x10, then sets Mission flags bit1.
claims.Limitations: Mission active flag is separate from per-widget active flag4.

claims.Finding: Stops all registered widgets via vtable+24 and clears Mission flags bit1.
claims.Limitations: Do not restart timers when the mission's native UI/control set is intentionally stopped.

claims.Finding: Calls widget stop when active and sets flag0x10 to suppress subsequent automatic activation.
claims.Limitations: Timer action rejects this state instead of overriding hidden/disabled native ownership.

claims.Finding: Mission phase0 starts widgets when its presentation permits; phase1 is the ordinary active state. Phase2 advances to3; phase3 sets up terminal presentation and advances4; phase4 eventually dispatches saved event+1076 and argument+1080, then ends its task.
claims.Limitations: Exact names of events7/16 are not inferred from the integers alone.

claims.Finding: Member-style lifecycle updater mirrors3A35C0 and passes both saved event and argument to3A3540; returns false after terminal dispatch.
claims.Limitations: Only scheduler-registered3A35C0 is relied on for the current native path.

claims.Finding: Returns true when current mission exists and Mission flags bit4 is clear.
claims.Limitations: This native gate alone is weaker than trainer guards: it does not prove phase1, initialized timer, pause state or scene safety.

claims.Finding: Tests only whether global current mission pointer is nonnull.
claims.Limitations: Presence is not resource/configuration readiness.

claims.Finding: Returns current Mission pointer without validation.
claims.Limitations: Module uses direct checked reads; it does not expose this pointer to users.

claims.Finding: Loader cleanup clears current mission pointer and descriptor mirror.
claims.Limitations: Mission destructor does not alone clear every resource field in static storage.

claims.Finding: Teardown stops clock, applies mission-specific cleanup, destroys script/effect resource handles, releases BAR and nulls current mission. Certain mission IDs also check counters for a Steam achievement before cleanup.
claims.Limitations: Counter edits can influence achievements; mission data is not merely a display.

claims.Finding: Returns Mission+1704 float if a mission exists, otherwise1.
claims.Limitations: Corrects earlier shorthand: RVA2A0FF68 is Mission, not a generic area structure. No new Drive control is implemented here.

claims.Finding: Tests descriptor flag0x1000 from Mission+8,+4.
claims.Limitations: Root separately studies how this gates retry checkpoint creation; this module does not change it.

claims.Finding: Reports whether Mission flags0x10 is clear, or true if no mission exists.
claims.Limitations: This is a control/finish gate, not an independent lifecycle generation.

claims.Finding: ORs supplied mask into Mission+1696 when mission exists.
claims.Limitations: Potential future standard-gauge-update hold; no persistent mask override implemented.

claims.Finding: Clears only supplied mask from Mission+1696.
claims.Limitations: A future lease must preserve other owners and account for mission reconstruction, direct setter bypasses and third-party writers.

claims.Finding: Activates counter flag4 and creates optional HUD bound to live value+56 and maximum+36. Existing completed flag8 selects completed presentation.
claims.Limitations: Readouts never dereference the HUD pointer.

claims.Finding: Activates gauge flag4, copies float(initial+32) into live+56 and creates an optional gauge HUD using max+36.
claims.Limitations: Repeating activation resets data and presentation; not used as a generic refresh.

claims.Finding: Timer activation sets widget active4 and may create HUD. Initial+32>0 selects countdown; otherwise max+36 selects count-up; starts global clock and clears pause owner2.
claims.Limitations: Trainer requires already-active timer, so its restart wrapper never takes this allocation/HUD initialization branch.

claims.Finding: Timer stop hides the HUD, sets shared clock pause owner2 and clears widget active4.
claims.Limitations: Clock pause mask and widget active state are independent; both are gated.

claims.Finding: Counter stop destroys its optional HUD pointer, zeros that pointer and clears active4.
claims.Limitations: Its configured value may remain readable from a registered widget.

claims.Finding: Gauge stop tells its HUD to stop and clears active4.
claims.Limitations: Unlike counter stop, the function does not explicitly zero stored HUD pointer; no trainer dereference.

claims.Finding: Stores initial+32 and threshold+40; nonzero max argument masks off0x40000000 into maximum+36 and translates that bit into widget display flag2.
claims.Limitations: Raw maximum arguments may encode mode bits; trainer reads the already-decoded runtime maximum.

claims.Finding: Counter configuration additionally initializes live integer value+56 from initial argument.
claims.Limitations: Constructor-only fields are excluded by registry membership.

claims.Finding: Integer counter setter clamps0..maximum and emits event123 with counterID on reaching maximum from below, or event14 on crossing tozero. Threshold direction depends on initial relative to threshold; crossing toggles completion via virtual+32/+40, then stores value.
claims.Limitations: Events execute before final value write and can run arbitrary registered script/progression handlers. No mutable counter trainer command yet.

claims.Finding: Float gauge setter clamps0..maximum and emits event136 atzero or137 atmaximum. Threshold test truncates float toint and calls completion/reset virtuals before storing float+56.
claims.Limitations: NaN inputs are not a valid trainer contract; mutable gauges deferred because of synchronous event/lifecycle effects.

claims.Finding: Counter completion updates optional HUD, plays configured sound if newly completed while active, and sets widget flag8.
claims.Limitations: Flag8 is threshold presentation/completion state, not universal mission success.

claims.Finding: Gauge completion updates HUD, conditionally plays configured sound and sets flag8.
claims.Limitations: Different missions can interpret gauge boundary events differently.

claims.Finding: Native set-counter wrapper ABI is integer valueECX,indexEDX. Requires live non-ended mission and widget flag1, then3FA230.
claims.Limitations: No native index bounds check; trainer does not expose this setter.

claims.Finding: Native gauge setter ABI float XMM0,indexEDX checks current mission active and Mission+1696==0, then calls3FA310 with objectRCX and float XMM1.
claims.Limitations: This mask suppresses the standard mission setter only; direct3FA310 initialization paths can bypass it.

claims.Finding: Ratio setter multiplies requested float by configured maximum then invokes3FBCB0.
claims.Limitations: Not implemented; same synchronous boundary events remain.

claims.Finding: Gauge-add wrapper applies mission-name-specific half scaling when global delta717480<2, then adds to existing float value and calls3FBCB0. Names includePO01_MS501,TT12_WORK_BOX,HB32_FM_VEX,TR04_MS104/TR07_MS203 andEH15_MS104.
claims.Limitations: Threshold constants are preserved in fresh byte evidence; do not assume all gauge changes have a universal rate or unit.

claims.Finding: Counter getter uses signed index and returns Mission+352+80*index+56 when present and flag1.
claims.Limitations: Trainer bounds0..2 and checks registry, ID, class and numeric bounds instead of trusting this weak getter.

claims.Finding: Gauge ratio getter divides live float+56 by integer maximum+36.
claims.Limitations: Native does not guard max0; trainer publishes raw value and maximum separately without dividing.

claims.Finding: Timer getter checks configured flag then returns global clock display through3FA0A0/157080.
claims.Limitations: Mission has one shared native clock; not a separate timer per index.

claims.Finding: Timer seconds getter rounds integer display upward with(value+59)/60.
claims.Limitations: Trainer exposes fractional engine seconds usingvalue/60, explicitly a different display precision.

claims.Finding: Native restart ABI char __fastcall(int secondsECX,int indexEDX). Requires non-ended mission and timer flag1; inactive timer would be activated via virtual+16. Negative seconds substitute configured max+36. Existing active timer directly calls3FA5D0.
claims.Limitations: Trainer only passes index0 and seconds0 or1..3599, verifies active widget, and never interprets AL as success.

claims.Finding: seconds>0 invokes157140(countdown); seconds<=0 invokes157170(timer+36 count-up limit); then157190starts and157110(2)clears script/timer pause owner.
claims.Limitations: Trainer rejects any existing pause mask before calling, avoiding appropriation of native bit2. Current direction is not a required precondition.

claims.Finding: ECX seconds is multiplied by60 in32-bit; sets mode1, phase0 and both duration/display frames.
claims.Limitations: Trainer countdown range1..3599 avoids overflow and the ordinary HUD's one-hour branch.

claims.Finding: ECX configured limit seconds multiplied by60; sets mode0, phase0, display0 and duration frames.
claims.Limitations: Existing nonnegative limits up to35791394 are accepted; zero is unbounded by configured deadline.

claims.Finding: Copies current global tick counter to origin and sets phase1 (armed).
claims.Limitations: Native update consumes one armed update before ordinary elapsed calculation; no asynchronous trainer queue.

claims.Finding: Clears supplied bits from global pause mask ABB854.
claims.Limitations: Native restart clears only bit2; module does not directly write pause bits.

claims.Finding: Sets supplied bits in global pause mask ABB854.
claims.Limitations: Existing World field pause uses a separate trainer bit0x40000000; Mission restart refuses all nonzero masks.

claims.Finding: Increments global clock tick counter only when entire pause mask iszero.
claims.Limitations: Counter is32-bit and may wrap; restart preserves its native unsigned bit pattern.

claims.Finding: Update ignores all paused states; armed1 becomes running2. Countdown computesduration+origin-tick and stops atzero with event74,arg0. Count-up computes tick-origin, caps at215999 before checking configured positive limit, and stops with event74 when a representable limit is reached.
claims.Limitations: Count-up limits above215999frames never reach their timeout branch after display cap; this is native behavior, preserved and documented.

claims.Finding: Stops the clock byphase0 and returns last displayed frames.
claims.Limitations: Trainer rejects stopped clocks because timeout/end dispatch may already have begun; no timeout resurrection.

claims.Finding: Returns displayed native clock frames fromABB860.
claims.Limitations: No wall-clock timing guarantee; engine units are60ticks per second.

claims.Finding: Initializes global clock state and registers1571B0 group0 priority1 on application scheduler.
claims.Limitations: Timer action does not recreate scheduler tasks.

claims.Finding: Timing callback increments mission clock through1570F0 and native frame counters, then signals timing semaphore.
claims.Limitations: A rendering/simulation scheduling system drives this callback; not a trainer-owned real-time timer.

claims.Finding: Registers154700 as timing callback, initializes global timer scheduler and adds1548E0 final timing task priority800000.
claims.Limitations: Uses existing app scheduling; no additional hook introduced.

claims.Finding: HUD update reads current display157080 and countdown mode1570D0 dynamically, so an active timer can change direction without rebuilding its HUD. Last-seconds warning effects set latch bits atHUD+7824; this restart route does not clear them.
claims.Limitations: Already-triggered final-seconds warnings may not play again after restarting. Normal numeric update excludes nonzerohours; no promise to reset every cosmetic state.

claims.Finding: VM callback reads lowinteger of first8-byte argument and second at+8, passes secondsECX,indexEDX to3FB9A0.
claims.Limitations: Trainer invokes typed native wrapper directly with fixed index0; it does not manufacture VM operand buffers.

claims.Finding: Script timer-pause callback requests clock ownerbit2.
claims.Limitations: Module refuses to clear this native owner's pause implicitly.

claims.Finding: Script timer-resume callback releases clock ownerbit2.
claims.Limitations: Existing script controls continue unchanged.

claims.Finding: Event dispatcher removes matching pending event records, then routes ordinary mission events to eight script contexts3F4980, Actor callback traversal3B4270 and registered condition handler3F60D0 synchronously.
claims.Limitations: Counter/gauge setters can mutate scripts, Actors, progress and scene before returning. No universal safe 'win/lose' setter is claimed.

claims.Finding: Packages event and parameter as two typed8-byte integer VM operands and calls script entry10 on each of8 registered contexts.
claims.Limitations: External BDX contents determine additional effects.

claims.Finding: Broadcasts the event/argument to every native Actor through controller vtable+96.
claims.Limitations: Uses native linked traversal; a generic external event call requires actor-list validation beyond timer restart.

claims.Finding: Searches16 condition-handler records of96bytes by event and argument, preferring exact argument while retaining a wildcard match when either argument isnegative.
claims.Limitations: Condition predicates and handler outcomes cannot be inferred solely from event numbers.

claims.Finding: Finds a matching condition record, applies3F61A0 progression effects, then either returns handled, starts an event, or applies a destination/map change.
claims.Limitations: This makes counter/gauge mutation potentially persistent and scene-changing.

claims.Finding: Handler side effects can set progression flags, call progression helpers3E3930 and3A1A60/3A1E70 for listed records, and update encoded flags; finally marks handler event-1 to consume it.
claims.Limitations: Not just an in-memory display effect; mutable counter/gauge commands remain open research.

claims.Finding: Routes ordinary completion to3A41E0 event7; for descriptor mode30 and an already-set matching event7 progression flag, selects event156 instead.
claims.Limitations: Do not label a direct call universally safe victory; reward and story semantics are mission-specific.

claims.Finding: Routes to same completion common function3A41E0 with event16 and caller argument.
claims.Limitations: Distinct terminal presentation, not enough evidence to equate16 with universal failure.

claims.Finding: Before terminal presentation, applies descriptor bonus level through3EDCA0, optionally gives score time bonus and score-derived EXP, plays sound, marks Mission flags0x14, stops clock and changes input/event state. Saves event and argument for phase2/4 or immediatelydispatches.
claims.Limitations: Direct 'complete mission' would invoke progression, external handlers and resource lifetime changes. Not implemented.

claims.Finding: Terminal dispatcher forwards event and preserved argument into3AABE0. A handled result destroys mission; unhandled event8 routes to3A3910; special modes/156 open result menu.
claims.Limitations: Boolean handled is event routing status, not proof of a universal successful win.

claims.Finding: Failure/abort path stops clock and applies control locks, then schedules event8 presentation/handler or tears down and chooses restart/gameover menu paths.
claims.Limitations: Root owns deeper Game-over/Mickey analysis. Mission module does not synthesize this event.

claims.Finding: Score setup sets value0,max9999 and stores scoring unit+592, EXP cap+596 and time bonus+600, then activates presentation.
claims.Limitations: Score values are bounded0..9999 in readouts.

claims.Finding: Adds amount*configuredunit to score via native counter setter3FA230.
claims.Limitations: Score edits would also bypass expected activity statistics; no writer implemented.

claims.Finding: Adds configured time bonus to score through3FA230.
claims.Limitations: Completion calls this if native timer getter ispositive.

claims.Finding: Tracks128 typedID entries with a one-byte count. Matching entry returns oldcount then increments thebyte; replacement chooses the lowest-countentry.
claims.Limitations: Repetition history is separate from total score and can wrap its byte counter. No modification implemented.

claims.Finding: Award from one resource type uses2^-repetition * its ushort value, with zero result promotedto1, then updates score.
claims.Limitations: Names of resource classes remain unasserted here; this is a diminishing repeat-reward mechanism.

claims.Finding: Parallel award route uses a second typed repetition bank and a different ushort resource field before the same score setter.
claims.Limitations: Exact association with every minigame item is external-data dependent.

claims.Finding: Completion converts score to EXP as min(configuredcap, (unit+score-1)/unit) then calls3ECF30.
claims.Limitations: Native code divides without a zero guard. Trainer does not expose score/finish calls or manufacture invalid scoring configuration.

open_work: External mission BDX mapping: which concrete event14/74/123/136/137 means success, failure, progression, spawn or map change for each mission.
Mutable counter/gauge controls: validate complete synchronous event graph and loaded handler data, actor/list ownership, record bounds, reentrant resource lifetime and story effects before exposing.
Mission+1696 gauge standard-setter hold: native OR/AND owner mechanism is promising, but direct3FA310 calls bypass it; needs lifecycle/writer ownership proof and precise scope.
Native terminal events7/16/156: data-driven result semantics and reward safety not generalized into a universal force-win button.
HUD warning latch reset: not implemented; native already-active restart can retain final-seconds warning bits.
Mission identity uses pointer/descriptor/BAR/ID/registry/scene snapshots, not a global generation counter. Exact ABA between snapshots and unsupported concurrent mods remain unproven.
Runtime compatibility and actual mission scenes were not tested. Synthetic tests replace only the typed native callout and exercise memory/layout/gates.
